# Four-Week Coding Interview Prep in Java: Comprehensive Learning Guide

## Course Overview

This four-week intensive course is designed to equip mid-level Java developers with the algorithmic thinking and coding patterns essential for passing technical interviews at FAANG and tier-1 tech companies. The course bridges the gap between basic Java knowledge and interview-ready problem-solving, covering 98 curated practice tasks that mirror real interview questions.

**Who This Is For:**
- Java developers with 1–3 years of experience
- Career changers preparing for their first technical role
- Professionals upskilling for senior-level positions
- Anyone targeting competitive coding interviews

**Why It Matters:**
Technical interviews increasingly focus on demonstrating not just language syntax knowledge, but algorithmic reasoning, optimization skills, and ability to communicate solutions under pressure. This course compresses months of self-study into a focused four-week sprint, covering the high-frequency patterns and data structures that appear in 80% of interview questions.

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Arrays & Strings** – Manipulation, searching, sorting, and pattern matching with real-world constraints
- **Linked Lists** – Node-based structures, pointer manipulation, cycle detection, and reversal operations
- **Stacks & Queues** – LIFO/FIFO principles, monotonic stacks, and real-world application patterns
- **Hash Maps & Sets** – Frequency counting, collision handling, and two-pointer/sliding window optimization
- **Trees & Graphs** – Traversals (BFS, DFS), binary search trees, balanced trees, and graph algorithms
- **Dynamic Programming** – Memoization, tabulation, overlapping subproblems, and optimal substructure recognition
- **Sorting & Searching** – Binary search variants, merge sort, quicksort, and heap-based solutions
- **Advanced Patterns** – Sliding windows, two pointers, prefix sums, union-find, and backtracking

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### **Week 1: Foundations & Array/String Mastery**
**Focus:** Core data structures and foundational patterns (24 tasks)

**Days 1–2: Arrays Fundamentals**
- Two-pointer technique (reverse arrays, valid palindromes)
- Sliding window for subarrays (max sum, minimum window substring)
- Tasks: 6 problems on array manipulation, sorting variants, searching edge cases

**Days 3–4: String Patterns**
- String reversal, anagrams, and pattern matching
- Substring problems (longest substring without repeating characters)
- Tasks: 6 problems on string transformations and searches

**Days 5–7: Hash Map/Set Mastery**
- Frequency counting and group-by operations
- Character set problems and intersection/union operations
- Tasks: 12 problems emphasizing space-time tradeoffs

**Week 1 Deliverable:** Solve 24 problems. Target time: 15–20 minutes per problem. Focus on writing clean, optimized code with clear variable naming.

---

### **Week 2: Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues & Trees (Part 1)**
**Focus:** Non-array sequential structures (24 tasks)

**Days 1–2: Linked Lists**
- Node manipulation, reversal, and cycle detection
- Merge operations and reordering
- Tasks: 6 problems covering insertion, deletion, and traversal

**Days 3–4: Stacks & Queues**
- LIFO/FIFO applications (parenthesis matching, BFS with queues)
- Monotonic stacks for next greater element problems
- Tasks: 6 problems on stack-based optimizations

**Days 5–7: Trees – Traversals & Basic Operations**
- DFS (preorder, inorder, postorder) and BFS
- Binary search tree properties
- Level-order and path-based problems
- Tasks: 12 problems on tree construction, validation, and traversal

**Week 2 Deliverable:** Solve 24 problems. Emphasis on pointer/reference manipulation and recursive thinking. Practice explaining traversal order aloud.

---

### **Week 3: Graphs, Dynamic Programming & Advanced Patterns**
**Focus:** Complex graph algorithms and optimization techniques (28 tasks)

**Days 1–2: Graph Fundamentals**
- Adjacency list/matrix representation
- DFS and BFS for connected components
- Tasks: 4 problems on graph traversal and connectivity

**Days 3–4: Graph Algorithms**
- Topological sort, cycle detection in directed graphs
- Shortest path (Dijkstra, BFS for unweighted)
- Tasks: 6 problems on path-finding and cycle detection

**Days 5–6: Dynamic Programming – Part 1**
- Recognizing overlapping subproblems (Fibonacci, coin change)
- Memoization vs. tabulation tradeoffs
- 1D DP patterns
- Tasks: 8 problems on sequence optimization

**Day 7: Dynamic Programming – Part 2**
- 2D DP (longest common subsequence, matrix paths)
- Knapsack variants
- Tasks: 4 problems on matrix and sequence DP

**Bonus Pattern Problems** (6 tasks)
- Sliding window variants
- Two-pointer in sorted arrays
- Prefix sum optimizations

**Week 3 Deliverable:** Solve 28 problems. Write DP solutions both with memoization (top-down) and tabulation (bottom-up). Identify and explain time/space complexity reductions.

---

### **Week 4: Intensive Review, Harder Problems & Mock Interviews**
**Focus:** Integration, harder variants, and interview simulation (22 tasks)

**Days 1–3: Mixed Problem Solving**
- Solve 12 "medium-hard" problems combining 2–3 topics (e.g., graph + DP, tree + hash map)
- Time yourself: 25–35 minutes per problem
- Focus on first approach correctness, then optimization

**Days 4–5: Backtracking & Combinatorial Problems**
- Permutations, combinations, and constraint satisfaction
- N-Queens, Sudoku solver patterns
- Tasks: 6 problems

**Days 6–7: Mock Interview & Final Review**
- 2 full mock interview scenarios (90 minutes each)
- 4 curated "surprise" problems covering weak spots
- Code review and optimization pass

**Week 4 Deliverable:** Complete all 22 problems. Record yourself solving one problem aloud to identify communication gaps.

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### **Algorithmic Thinking**
- Recognizing problem patterns and applicable algorithms
- Breaking complex problems into subproblems
- Identifying time/space tradeoffs and choosing optimal solutions

### **Code Optimization**
- Recognizing O(n²) bottlenecks and reducing to O(n log n) or O(n)
- Memory management and avoiding unnecessary data structures
- Writing code that passes edge cases on the first try

### **Communication Under Pressure**
- Articulating your approach before coding
- Explaining trade-offs clearly
- Handling clarifying questions and constraints adjustments

### **Debugging & Validation**
- Writing test cases mentally before coding
- Tracing through examples by hand
- Spotting off-by-one errors and null pointer issues

### **Pattern Recognition**
- Identifying when sliding window applies
- Recognizing DP substructure
- Knowing when to use hash maps vs. sorting vs. trees

---

## Sample Problem Types

### **Problem Type 1: Sliding Window**
**Description:** Find the longest substring with at most k distinct characters.

**Approach:** Two pointers with hash map to track character frequencies. Expand right pointer, shrink left when constraint violated.
